title: Middle East war, high debt levels to dominate IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
gist: The October 2026 IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok convene under the US-Israeli war with Iran, Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz (the biggest-ever energy supply shock), rising rates and record public debt. Officials hold ~3% 2026 global growth but warn of compounding diesel, fertilizer and El Niño shocks, thinning accessible oil inventories, and acute debt stress in emerging markets facing $400 billion in external payments.

themes.theme: Hormuz energy shock and oil inventories

insights.so_what: The largest-ever energy supply shock underpins elevated oil and refined-product prices and inflation risk.

insights.claim: The IMF says global public debt is at its highest level since World War Two and will exceed 100% of GDP before 2030, sapping growth and adding inflationary pressure.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Heavy sovereign issuance and fiscal dominance risk keep upward pressure on bond yields.
